document: The executable closure of the M6 Gate B transaction/restart equivalence campaign
note: The single source of truth for what the Gate B campaign is made of. The runner reads it to record the object identity of every path at the tree it actually ran on; the permanent verifier reads it to require those identities to still hold. Neither restates the list, because a list kept in two places is a list that will disagree.
rule: A change to anything here changes what the evidence is evidence of, so retained reports produced before the change may not be promoted after it: the campaign has to be run again. A change to anything not here — documentation, the changelog, or unrelated jobs in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — leaves retained evidence valid. The dedicated `.github/workflows/m6-gate-b.yml` is bound as one object, so changes to Gate B's provisioning or call layer invalidate Gate B evidence without binding the rest of CI.

workspace framework and adapter source.why: Every Gate B scenario runs the runtime and the PostgreSQL adapter this code declares, including the chunk transaction manager, the repository ports, and the recovery path B-04/B-05/B-06/B-07 drive directly.

migrations.why: The durable schema every Gate B scenario migrates the fixture database to before it runs.

campaign implementation.why: The exact test targets Gate B's frozen protocol names, plus the shared support module they all build on and the local crash-restore module that support reuses. A workspace test file not listed here is outside the campaign: it is not selected, so it is neither run nor able to affect the campaign's result.

cargo manifests.why: Feature selection and dependency ranges for every crate the campaign builds and runs. A campaign built with different features is a different campaign.

dependency resolution.why: The exact dependency graph every target the campaign runs was built from.

toolchain and build configuration.why: The compiler the campaign is built with, and the cargo configuration it is built under.

campaign fixtures.why: This closure document itself. Gate B's declared target/test scope is not a separate document (unlike the M5 crash-restore campaign's campaign-scope.json) -- it is the fixed constants xtask/src/gate_b.rs itself declares, already covered under "independent verifier" below, since Gate B's frozen eight-scenario protocol does not evolve the way an M5 multi-report campaign's accepted scope does.

Gate B execution contract.why: How CI actually runs the campaign: the supported PostgreSQL matrix, the database and maintenance connection it is given, the command, and the environment. The dedicated workflow is included with them, and its contract-check step fails closed if the workflow drifts from the contract. An unrelated CI job in ci.yml does not invalidate retained Gate B evidence, while any change to the dedicated Gate B workflow does.

independent verifier.why: The program that decides whether a run proved what it owed and whether retained evidence is still what it says. Its verdicts are part of the campaign result, so a report produced under a different verifier is a result under a different standard. Listed as the specific files that implement it, matching every M5 campaign's own closure: `main.rs` dispatches the command, `gate_b.rs` runs the fixed target/test scope and computes the execution manifest, `evidence.rs` is the permanent offline verifier, and `suite.rs` is the target-running and libtest-parsing mechanics every runner shares.
